lawyer:
Dr. Rafiqur Rahman with Md. Ismail Khan, Advocates ------- For the Petitioners. 
Fakhrul Islam, AAG  ------- For the Respondent No.2
parties:
Jalil and another  ------- Petitioner 
Vs. 
The Chairman, Court of Settlement and another ------- Respondents.
full_judgment:
8. The learned Court of Settlement relied on Section 5(2) of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance, 1985 and gave its decision in favour of the Government on the basis of presumption. 

 10. He further submits that the presumption under section 5(2) of the said Ordinance is not conclusive and at least the Government must show the basis of treating the said property as abandoned property and as to how this property comes within the definition of the abandoned property. He further submits that in any view of the matter the petitioners having asserted that they were in the disputed house since 1974 when they were forcibly evicted along with their mother, the owner of the house, and this assertion having not been denied by the Government side and there being no finding on that point, the assertion of the petitioner it is to be treated as correct and in that event the said property is not covered by the definition of abandoned property within the meaning of President Order No. 16 of 1972. 

 11. Mr. Fakrul Islam, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the respondent No. 2, of the other hand, submits that as the property in question had been listed as abandoned property and was published in the official Gazette under sub/section (I) of the section 5 of the said Ordinance, the presumption is that it is an abandoned property unless it is rebutted by evidence on behalf of the claimant to the satisfaction of the Court of Settlement. He further submits that as the Court of Settlement was not satisfied with the evidence led by the petitioners and the learned Court came to the finding that presumption was not rebutted the impugned order was passed with lawful authority. 

 13. So it is apparent that the burden is on the claimant of the property listed as abandoned property under section 5(2) of the said Ordinance to prove that it is not an abandoned property. The Court of Settlement disbelieved the evidence of the petitioners on the point that Alimunnessa the owner was buried on 10.3.75 in Mohammadpur graveyard and came to the finding that the petitioners failed to disprove the stand of the respondents that Aliman was not present in Bangladesh on 28.2.72 or near about it, far less proving that the claims of the petitioner's title to the case property is immune from the perilous effect of PO 16 of 1972. The learned Court relied on the presumption of section 5(2) of the said Ordinance. Section 10(5) of the said Ordinance provides that a Court of Settlement shall, after such enquiry as it may deem necessary and after giving reasonable opportunity to the parties concerned of being heard and of adducing evidence, both oral and documentary, if any, make such decision on the prayer of the applicant as it deems fit. 

 14. The presumption of correctness of the entries in the Gazette Notification does not absolve the Government from denying the fact alleged by the claimant or from disclosing the basis of treating the property as abandoned property when it is disputed. The abandoned property has been defined in Article 2(1) of PO 16 of 1972. If a property is covered by that definition it is an abandoned property. 

 16. It was the case of the petitioners that they and their mother the admitted owner of the property, had been living in the disputed house till June, 1974 when they were forcibly evicted. They also led evidence in support of said facts which was not denied by the Government. The learned Court of Settlement failed to take notice of the said position and failed to come to any finding on that point. Had this aspect of the case been taken notice of the presumption under section 5(2) of the said Ordinance would have been found to have been rebutted in spite of the fact that the court disbelieved the case of the petitioners about burial of Alimunnessa in Mohammadpur graveyard on 10.3.75. So there is no reason for treating the said property as abandoned property and the presumption of correctness under section 5(2) of the Ordinance has been amply rebutted.
